title: The Growing Infrastructure Resilience Opportunity for MSPs
summary: Learn how MSPs turn infrastructure resilience into recurring revenue with a five-step framework for protection, governance, and AI readiness. Read more.
body_markdown:
AI adoption, escalating cyberthreats, regulatory scrutiny, and cloud complexity have exposed a critical reality: Innovation only moves as fast as the resilience of the infrastructure supporting it.


Organizations are expanding across Microsoft 365, Azure, SaaS applications, data platforms, and increasingly AI-powered services. Yet many are struggling to maintain visibility, governance, recovery readiness, and operational consistency across those environments.[According to IDC](https://my.idc.com/getdoc.jsp?containerId=US52640724) , more than 60% of businesses are expected to modernize up to half of their cloud architecture to improve efficiency and enable innovation. This modernization creates new demands for governance, protection, optimization, and operational efficiency.


For managed service providers (MSPs), this represents a growing opportunity to transform infrastructure management into a portfolio of recurring, high-value managed services.


## Resilience Is No Longer Just About Recovery


Historically, backup, recovery, and business continuity were often treated as insurance policies. Customers viewed them as necessary operational expenses rather than strategic investments.


That mindset is changing. As customers continue to expand across cloud platforms faster than they can govern and operationalize them, infrastructure becomes increasingly distributed, and operational teams remain constrained by staffing shortages, complexity, and growing business expectations. Furthermore,[Gartner forecasts](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2024-09-18-gartner-says-30-percent-of-enterprises-will-automate-more-than-half-of-their-network-activities-by-2026) that only 30% of enterprises will automate more than half of their network activities in 2026, indicating that a significant amount of infrastructure management remains manual and operationally intensive.


Infrastructure resilience now spans:


- Data protection
- Backup and recovery
- Governance
- Security posture management
- Compliance oversight
- Cost optimization
- Identity controls
- AI readiness


Customers need confidence that their business can continue operating despite cyberattacks, outages, governance failures, compliance gaps, runaway cloud costs, or AI-related risks. The MSPs that customers trust most are not only focused on backup and disaster recovery but also on preventing risk, maintaining compliance, optimizing operations, and supporting innovation without compromising control.


## Why Infrastructure Resilience Has Become a Revenue Opportunity


The traditional MSP model has often centered on managing environments, responding to incidents, and supporting day-to-day operations. But customers are increasingly looking for proactive partners who can help them build resilient infrastructure.


MSPs can[build profitable infrastructure services](https://www.avepoint.com/blog/msp-and-channel/msp-profitable-infrastructure-services) by modernizing, protecting, governing, operating, and optimizing customer environments through a single standardized delivery model, rather than responding to problems on a project-by-project basis. Repeatable services across cloud operations, resilience, governance, optimization, and AI readiness let revenue scale faster than headcount.


Standardization is the first step. Without alignment at a foundational level, automation amplifies inconsistency rather than eliminating it.[AvePoint’s Road to AI Readiness report](https://www.avepoint.com/ebooks/ai-opportunity-governance-msp-research) finds 91% of MSPs say integrating backup and disaster recovery with data governance and compliance delivers stronger customer value than offering them separately.


## What Are Infrastructure Managed Services?


Infrastructure managed services help MSPs deliver, operate, and optimize customer environments through a proactive, always-on service model. As organizations expand across Microsoft 365, Azure, SaaS applications, and AI workloads, these services go beyond monitoring.


Infrastructure managed services help MSPs:


- **Strengthen resilience** through protection, recovery, and continuity services.
- **Improve operational efficiency** with standardized management and automation.
- **Support modernization and AI readiness** with secure, governed, and scalable infrastructure.
- **Reduce complexity** through centralized visibility and control across customer environments.


In essence, infrastructure managed services enable MSPs to deliver measurable business outcomes, helping customers reduce risk, improve uptime, and build a trusted foundation for innovation and AI adoption in a proactive way.


## AI Is Accelerating the Need for Infrastructure Resilience


The adoption of AI has accelerated reliance on data, making breaches potentially catastrophic for many customers.[According to GTIA](https://gtia.org/press-releases/new-gtia-study-reveals-cybersecurity-is-critical-but-under-prioritized-by-itsps) , 42% of IT service providers identify gaining and retaining customer trust around private data as a critical challenge — especially for MSPs with full access to sensitive information. The infrastructure that supports AI must be governed, protected, monitored, and recoverable.


[Omdia also forecasts](https://omdia.tech.informa.com/blogs/2025/sep/from-generative-ai-to-agentic-ai-the-us-276-billion-partner-opportunity) that the global partner opportunity tied to AI services will reach $267 billion by 2030, reflecting expanding enterprise investment in automation, data services, and AI-enabled workflows. But the majority of AI pilots fail, often because customers lack qualified in-house expertise, data privacy concerns, data quality issues, compliance and regulatory challenges, and integration difficulties with legacy systems.


The gap between AI ambition and operational readiness is widening across the channel, and not merely due to technical challenges. Demand is shifting toward integrated platforms over point solutions. The


[Road to AI Readiness report](https://www.avepoint.com/ebooks/ai-opportunity-governance-msp-research) identifies three priorities for MSPs looking to close the gap between AI demand and delivery: standardizing governance frameworks, improving multitenant visibility, and adopting unified data protection controls.


## Scale Infrastructure Resilience with Multitenant Management


Delivering infrastructure resilience to one customer is very different from delivering it consistently across dozens or hundreds of customer environments.


As the customer base grows, MSPs must manage different configurations, policies, subscriptions, workloads, and risk profiles. Without centralized visibility and standardized operations, service delivery becomes increasingly difficult and expensive to scale.


A[multitenant management platform](https://www.avepoint.com/products/elements) can help MSPs establish a consistent operating model across customer environments through:


- Centralized visibility across customer tenants.
- Standardized baseline configurations.
- Policy enforcement at scale.
- Configuration and policy drift detection.
- Consistent protection and governance controls.
- Centralized monitoring and reporting.
- Integration with professional services automation (PSA) and remote monitoring and management (RMM) tools.


These capabilities enable MSPs to deliver infrastructure services at scale through a standardized operating model. With centralized visibility, baseline configuration management, policy enforcement, drift detection, and reporting, MSPs can manage multiple customer environments efficiently while still meeting each organization’s unique requirements. Integration with PSA and RMM tools further streamlines operations and improves service consistency.


## Customers Need Outcomes, Not More Tools


Many organizations already own the technologies needed to improve resilience. What they lack is operational efficiency. Tool sprawl remains a major challenge across Microsoft 365, Azure, and SaaS environments. Different business units adopt infrastructure services independently. Policies drift over time. Backup coverage becomes inconsistent. Recovery processes grow more complex.


This five-step framework can help build a predictable infrastructure services business:


1. **Assess.** Identify customer risks, operational gaps, governance weaknesses, and modernization opportunities.
2. **Protect.** Implement protection, recovery, and continuity services that reduce risk and improve resilience.
3. **Govern.** Deliver ongoing compliance, security monitoring, and AI readiness solutions.
4. **Optimize.** Help customers reduce waste, improve performance, and maximize infrastructure investments.
5. **Scale.** Standardize delivery and automate operations to improve profitability without increasing headcount at the same rate.


By following this model, MSPs can move from one-off infrastructure projects to scalable services that deliver ongoing customer value, improve operational efficiency, and create more predictable revenue.
